prize_parts.citation: For a visionary prose and poetry in Romanian that turns memory, the body and dream into an inner cosmos of rare formal ambition and imaginative depth.

statement.case_for: My opening view holds. On the common criteria, Cărtărescu offers the most distinctive voice on the shortlist, the kind that can be recognised in the writing and nowhere else. Public knowledge of Blinding (the Orbitor trilogy) and Solenoid points to a densely patterned visionary prose in which memory, the body and dream become a sustained metaphysical project. Formal ambition is high and the imaginative world is internally coherent across volumes. The poetry origin and the essays give the oeuvre generic breadth beyond the large novels. A single-author citation is straightforward and rests on literary invention, not on national or political symbolism. The decades-long body of work looks consolidated, and the later books appear to extend the project in scale rather than simply repeat it. I am making this judgment from public knowledge and have not independently verified the texts.
statement.case_against: The strongest reservation is that so much of the evidence reaches us through translation. The density, rhythm and long sentence architecture of the Romanian may be only partly conveyed. The case also rests more on the large novels than on the poetry and shorter prose, which are thinner in translation. Encyclopedic length and recurring motifs can read as a strength or as self-enclosure, and I cannot rule out repetition across the late volumes without a close reading of the whole corpus. If the committee judged that the late work closes in on itself rather than deepening, the case would weaken considerably.

responses.point: Olsson ranks Zurita first. He argues that Purgatory and Anteparadise turn suffering and historical rupture into a sustained poetic form, that the voice is unmistakable, and that the landscape-scale interventions are a secondary extension of the written oeuvre.
responses.response: I agree this is the strongest poetry case among the candidates, which is why Zurita stands in my top three and among my alternatives. I accept the chair's framing that the citation must rest on the written poems, with the landscape work treated only as an extension. Two things keep me from moving him to first place. First, the achievement lies in sequence, scale and sound, which translation reduces more severely for poetry than for Cărtărescu's prose, so our shared evidence for the Spanish is weaker. Second, I want to see that the force of the work does not depend on its historical occasion. This is not a dispute about Zurita's merit but about how securely the committee can document it.

responses.point: Sward ranks Tawada second, arguing that writing in Japanese and German makes linguistic estrangement an inventive method across fiction, poetry, essays and drama. She also notes the difficulty of judging sustained scale from short, fragmentary forms.
responses.response: Tawada is a serious case on formal and linguistic achievement, and I should say plainly that I did not rank her in my opening. My knowledge of her work, and of how the German and Japanese bodies of work relate, is thinner than for the candidates I ranked. I share Sward's own reservation about sustained scale and depth across short forms. I do not think those reservations disqualify her, but I cannot yet say her oeuvre outweighs the ones I know better. If colleagues who read both languages or know the German work can show depth across the corpus, I would revisit her. I would also note that Cărtărescu's project is also built on language and consciousness, but at an architectural scale that Tawada's does not attempt.

responses.point: Sem-Sandberg ranks Cărtărescu first but flags that some late work may be too self-enclosed or repetitive in its motifs. He ranks Yan Lianke second, with the case resting on mythorealism and formal invention rather than testimony.
responses.response: The self-enclosure concern is the strongest challenge to my own preference, and I do not dismiss it. Where it matters most is whether Solenoid and later works deepen the project or only extend its machinery. I read the recurring motifs as the architecture of a personal mythology rather than as mere repetition, but that is a judgment from public knowledge and I could be wrong. On Yan Lianke, I agree that the case must be literary, not a matter of censorship, and the grotesque and mythic forms of The Four Books and The Explosion Chronicles are inventive. I ranked him sixth because I am less sure that quality holds across so many titles and because the language games are hard to judge in translation. That is a reservation about evidence, not a dismissal.

responses.point: Carlberg ranks Cărtărescu first and values the voice and the large architectures, but notes that the very long volumes mean the measure of the whole may depend on which books a reader knows. She ranks NDiaye fourth and questions whether her breadth matches the most monumental candidates.
responses.response: I accept her point about the length of the volumes. It argues for the committee reading the whole corpus, including the poetry and the earlier prose, before treating the novels as the oeuvre. I agree on NDiaye that breadth is the open question. I rank her second because the control, the unsettling tone and the range across fiction and drama are of a very high order. But her oeuvre is more compact than Cărtărescu's, and I cannot assess the drama directly. So I keep her as an alternative, not as my preferred laureate.

uncertainties: How much of the Romanian prose style, including rhythm, syntax and register, survives translation, and whether translated editions fairly represent the poetry, essays and earlier work.
Whether the late volumes deepen the project or only extend its scale and motifs.
Whether the committee can read the most translation-sensitive candidates (Zurita, Tawada, Michon, Couto, Adonis) in the original, and how that would shift the comparison.
How to weigh Zurita's non-textual landscape interventions within Nobel's framework, if the committee takes up his case.
My assessments rest on public knowledge of representative works and not on fresh reading or independent verification, so my view of the full bibliography may be incomplete.
statement.conflict_note: None apparent from the supplied profile. The profile lists no personal, institutional or translation connection to any shortlisted writer. My own practice as a historical and psychological novelist is context and not evidence of preference.
